name: Kettlebell Bottoms-Up Press
description: The kettlebell bottoms-up press inverts the kettlebell so the bell faces upward above the handle, requiring intense grip and forearm engagement to keep the bell stabilized throughout the press. The unstable inverted position activates the rotator cuff and scapular stabilizers far more than conventional pressing, making it an exceptional shoulder health and stability exercise. The unilateral nature also develops anti-rotation core strength.

execution.starting_position: Hold a kettlebell by the handle with the bell inverted (pointing up), arm at shoulder height. The wrist must be straight and directly under the bell to maintain balance. Begin with a light kettlebell.
execution.setup_instructions: Start with 25-35% of normal press load. The balance demand changes the nature of the exercise entirely. This can be performed standing, seated, or kneeling.
steps: Step 1: Grip the kettlebell handle firmly with the bell balanced above.
Step 2: Bring the bell to shoulder height with elbow at 90 degrees.
Step 3: Press directly overhead, keeping the bell balanced at all times.
Step 4: At lockout, the arm is fully extended with the bell balanced above.
Step 5: Lower under full control to the starting position.
execution.breathing_instructions: Exhale on the press, inhale on the descent.
common_mistakes: Using too heavy a kettlebell — balance failure is the limiting factor initially
Flaring the elbow wide — keep it slightly forward in the press
Bracing insufficiently against the unilateral load
safety_considerations: Have a plan if the kettlebell falls — step away from it rather than catching it
Begin over a padded surface when learning
execution.range_of_motion_guidance: Shoulder height to full lockout overhead.
coaching_cues: Tight grip — the bell tells you when you're losing it
Keep your wrist stacked under the bell
